Potato Sprouts: Potato sprouts are a joke block added in 24w14potato.
Potato flower: Potato flowers are decorative flowers that generate naturally in the Potato in 24w14potato.
Potato Stairs: Potato stairs are a potato variant of the wooden stairs, crafted from the respective potato planks, added in 24w14potato.
Potato Stem: A potato stem is a joke log-type block, only present in 24w14potato.
Potato Trapdoor: A potato trapdoor is a variant of a trapdoor made of potato planks in 24w14potato.
Potent Sulfur: Potent sulfur is a naturally generated block in sulfur caves at the bottom of sulfur pools and sulfur springs that produces noxious gas in and on top of water when placed under it. Noxious gas inflicts the player with 4 seconds of Nausea.
Potone: Potone is a common stone type block found underground in the Potato dimension in 24w14potato.
Potone Copper Ore: Potone copper ore is a type of ore found in the Potato dimension in 24w14potato.
Potone Diamond Ore: Potone diamond ore is a type of ore found in the Potato dimension in 24w14potato.
Potone Gold Ore: Potone gold ore is a type of ore found in the Potato dimension in 24w14potato.
Potone Iron Ore: Potone iron ore is a type of ore found in the Potato dimension in 24w14potato.
Potone Lapis Lazuli Ore: Potone lapis lazuli ore is a type of ore found in the Potato dimension in 24w14potato.
Potone Redstone Ore: Potone redstone ore is a type of ore found in the Potato dimension, only present in 24w14potato.
Potone Slab: A potone slab is a potone variant of a slab, only present in 24w14potato.
Potone Stairs: Potone stairs are a potone variant of the stairs, added in 24w14potato.
Potone Wall: A potone wall is a potone variant of a wall, only present in 24w14potato.
Powder Snow: Powder snow is a non-solid block found in snowy slopes and groves, or collected from snowfall using cauldrons. It slows down and deals freezing damage to most entities within it. Wearing any leather armor prevents freezing, and worn leather boots allow powder snow to be walked on and climbed through. It can only be obtained using a bucket and melts when placed inside water.
Powered Rail: A powered rail is a type of rail that either increases or halts the velocity of minecarts depending on its power state, and can be used to accelerate a minecart from a standstill when placed facing a conductive block.
Powerful Potato: A powerful potato is a block which can be found in the Potato dimension in 24w14potato.
Pressure Plate: A pressure plate is a non-solid block that produces a redstone signal when stood on by an entity, with multiple variants that have different properties.
Prismarine: Prismarine is a type of stone that appears underwater in ocean ruins and ocean monuments. It periodically changes color between blue and green.
Prismarine Brick Slab: A prismarine brick slab is a decorative slab variant of prismarine bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Red Nether Brick Stairs: Red Nether brick stairs are a decorative stairs variant of red Nether bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Red Nether Brick Wall: A red Nether brick wall is a decorative wall variant of red Nether bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Red Nether Bricks: Red Nether bricks are a decorative variant of Nether bricks that do not naturally generate.
Red Sand: Red sand is a variant of sand found exclusively in badlands biomes. It can be used in place of sand in many crafting recipes, with the exception of concrete powder.
Red Sandstone: Red sandstone is a variant of sandstone. It comes in three other variants: cut red sandstone, chiseled red sandstone, and smooth red sandstone.
Red Sandstone Slab: A red sandstone slab is a decorative slab variant of red sandstone that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Red Sandstone Stairs: Red sandstone stairs are a decorative stairs variant of red sandstone that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Red Sandstone Wall: A red sandstone wall is a decorative wall variant of red sandstone that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Redstone Comparator:
A redstone comparator is a block that can produce a redstone signal from its front by reading chests, lecterns, copper bulbs, and similar blocks. It can also repeat a signal without changing its strength. 
It can also be set to either stop outputting a signal while its side input is receiving a stronger one (front torch off), or output a weaker signal based on its side input's signal strength (front torch on).
Redstone Dust:
Redstone dust is a mineral used in crafting, brewing, trimming, and as a placeable wire.
Redstone wire is a non-solid block that can transmit a redstone power signal up to 15 blocks in distance; signal strengths below 15 have reduced distance. Redstone wire can power blocks it is placed on or pointing at.
Redstone Lamp: A redstone lamp is a solid block that produces light while it is receiving redstone power.
Redstone Ore:
Redstone ore is the ore block from which redstone is obtained.
Deepslate redstone ore is a variant of redstone ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff blobs.
Redstone Repeater: A redstone repeater is a block that produces a full-strength redstone signal from its front while its back is powered, with four toggleable delay settings. It can also be locked into its current power state by directly powering its side with another repeater or a redstone comparator.
Redstone Torch: A redstone torch is a non-solid block that produces a full-strength redstone signal on all sides adjacent to it, except for its attached block, and can power the block directly above it. It deactivates while the block it is attached to is powered.
Reinforced Deepslate: Reinforced deepslate is a block that generates exclusively in ancient cities. It has high hardness, is immune to explosions, and cannot be pushed by pistons or obtained in Survival mode.
Reserved6: reserved6 is an unused former technical block. It was used for referencing empty inventory slots.
Resin Brick Slab: A resin brick slab is a decorative slab variant of resin bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Resin Brick Stairs: Resin brick stairs are a decorative stairs variant of resin bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Resin Brick Wall: A resin brick wall is a decorative wall variant of resin bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Resin Bricks: Resin bricks are a block crafted from resin brick. It can also be crafted into its block family, containing slabs, stairs, walls, and the chiseled variant.
Resin Clump: A resin clump is a block generated by a creaking heart on pale oaks in any biome when a creaking is attacked. It also drops when a creaking heart is mined or destroyed. It can be used to craft decorative blocks of resin, and can also be smelted to produce resin bricks, which in turn can be crafted into the whole resin brick block family.
Resin Ore:
Resin ore is a type of ore found in the Potato dimension in 24w14potato. 
Breaking resin ore drops one toxic resin, unless mined with a Silk Touch hoe. Toxic resin obtained from resin ore always has "air bubbles" impurities, and either "abysmal", "clouded", or "eventual" clarity. Resin ore is affected by Fortune enchantment, dropping an average of 1.33 toxic resins with level I, 1.75 toxic resins with level II, and 2.2 toxic resins with level III. All resins dropped from a single ore block always are of the same clarity.
Respawn Anchor: The respawn anchor is a block that allows the player to set their spawn point in the Nether. It will only work if fueled using glowstone blocks.
Rooted Dirt: Rooted dirt is a natural decorative block.
Rose Bush: A rose bush is a tall flower that can be crafted into red dye.
Sand: Sand is a gravity-affected block found abundantly in deserts and beaches, and less commonly in or near surface water.
Sandstone: Sandstone is a solid block related to sand that comes in two color variants, the other being red sandstone. Regular sandstone is commonly found in deserts and beaches. Sandstone also has three decorative variants: chiseled sandstone, cut sandstone, and smooth sandstone.
Sandstone Slab: A sandstone slab  is a decorative slab variant of sandstone that generates in desert structures and is used for building.
Sandstone Stairs: Sandstone stairs are a decorative stairs variant of sandstone that generates in overworld structures and is used for building.
Sandstone Wall: A sandstone wall is a decorative wall variant of sandstone that generates in desert villages and is used for building.
Sapling: A sapling is a non-solid block that can be grown into a tree.
Scaffolding: Scaffolding is a climbable semi-solid block with a stable top platform and unique placement controls that simplify creating columns and bridges. Scaffolding pieces fall downward if placed too far away from a supporting block, which can naturally form into more supporting columns.
Sculk: Sculk is a block found abundantly in the deep dark or converted from other blocks by a sculk catalyst. Like most of the rest of the sculk family, it drops experience when broken by a tool.
Sculk Catalyst: A sculk catalyst is a sculk block that "blooms" when a mob or player dies nearby, which may convert nearby blocks to sculk blocks (except for more sculk catalysts).
Sculk Sensor: A sculk sensor is a sculk block that detects vibrations caused by nearby actions and events and emits a redstone signal in response. Player-caused vibrations can also trigger nearby sculk shriekers. Sneaking prevents the creation of vibrations while moving, and wool can be used to block or prevent them. Placing an amethyst block next to a sculk sensor allows it to "relay" detected vibrations to other sculk sensors.
Sculk Shrieker:
A sculk shrieker is a sculk block that will "shriek" if any player touches its top (even indirectly) or activates a nearby sculk sensor. Only players can trigger it. 
Naturally-generated sculk shriekers also inflict Darkness and may summon a warden if triggered, but shriekers placed by players or sculk catalysts are completely inert and harmless.
Sculk Vein: A sculk vein is a block found in the deep dark or generated by sculk catalysts. It can generate or be placed on any side of a solid block.
Sea Lantern: A sea lantern is an underwater light source that appears in ocean monuments and ocean ruins.
Sea Pickle: A sea pickle is a block found in warm oceans. While in water it emits light, and can be spread using bone meal if placed on a living coral block. Up to four sea pickles can be placed in one block space, which affects the amount of light produced while in water.
Seagrass:
Seagrass is a non-solid plant block that generates in all oceans, except frozen oceans.
Tall seagrass is a two-block high variety of seagrass.
Prismarine Brick Stairs: Prismarine brick stairs are a decorative stairs variant of prismarine bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Prismarine Bricks: Prismarine bricks are a variant of prismarine, appearing as cyan bricks with chiseled patterns.
Prismarine Slab: A prismarine slab is a decorative slab variant of prismarine that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Prismarine Stairs: Prismarine stairs are a decorative stairs variant of prismarine that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Prismarine Wall: A prismarine wall is a decorative wall variant of prismarine that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Pumpkin: A pumpkin is a block found in patches in grassy biomes or grown from pumpkin seeds, which it can also be crafted into. Using shears on a pumpkin carves a face into it and drops pumpkin seeds.
Pumpkin Seeds:
Pumpkin seeds are items obtained from pumpkins that can be used to grow pumpkin stems.
Pumpkin stems are plants grown on farmland that, over time, grow pumpkins on dirt, mud and moss blocks adjacent to them.
Purpur Block: Purpur blocks are decorative blocks that can be crafted with popped chorus fruit and are naturally generated in End cities and End ships.
Purpur Pillar: Purpur pillars are decorative blocks that can be crafted with purpur slabs and are naturally generated in End cities and End ships.
Purpur Slab: A purpur slab is a decorative slab variant of purpur that generates in End cities and is used for building.
Purpur Stairs: Purpur stairs are a decorative stairs variant of purpur that generates in End cities and is used for building.
Quadruple Compressed Poisonous Potato Bl: A quadruple compressed poisonous potato block is a compacted block made of triple compressed poisonous potato blocks in 24w14potato.
Quartz Bricks: Quartz bricks are the brick variant of the block of quartz, obtained through crafting.
Quartz Pillar: A quartz pillar is a variant of the block of quartz, obtained through crafting.
Quartz Slab: A quartz slab is a decorative slab variant of quartz that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Quartz Stairs: Quartz stairs are a decorative stairs variant of quartz that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Quiz Block: A quiz block was a block used to set up student quizzes.
Rail:
A rail is a non-solid block that provides a path along which minecarts can travel, and can be placed either flat on the ground, as a ramp, or curved.
A curved rail allows minecarts to turn corners, and can rotate to connect to a different rail line while powered.
Red Mushroom: A red mushroom is a variety of fungus that grows and spreads in dark areas. Mushrooms can generate small or huge in size.
Red Nether Brick Slab: A red Nether brick slab is a decorative slab variant of red Nether bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Seamless Stone Slab: A seamless stone slab refers to several unused variants of the slab block with metadata exceeding what was actually used at the time. They can be considered a precursor to smooth stone.
Shelf: A shelf is a block that can store and display up to three stacks of items. A shelf can be used to swap its slots with the slots in the player's hotbar. It swaps 1 slot normally, and 3 slots at a time when powered with redstone.
Shimmering Door: Shimmering door is a block added in 25w14craftmine.
Short Dry Grass: Short dry grass is a one-block tall foliage block that generates frequently in deserts and all types of badlands. It grows on sand and terracotta. It can also be eaten by sheep.
Short Grass: Short grass is a non-solid plant block that may drop wheat seeds when broken. Its color is biome-dependent, and matches the color of grass blocks.
Shroomlight: Shroomlights are light-emitting blocks that generate in huge fungi.
Shrub: The shrub is an unused variant of short grass exclusive to the Legacy Console Edition that does not generate naturally. It was also present in both Java and Bedrock editions, where, in the latter, it used the name fern and took the appearance of short grass.
Shulker Box: A shulker box is a dyeable block that stores items, and, unlike all other storage blocks, keeps its contents in item form when broken.
Sign: A sign is a non-solid block that can display text, and can be placed on the top or side of other blocks. The text of signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent its text from being edited by any player.
Six-sided Piston: A six-sided piston was an extreme metadata variant of the piston. It could be used as update suppression agents.
Skeleton Skull: A skeleton skull is the head of a skeleton in the form of a block. It can be obtained from ancient cities or by killing a skeleton using a charged creeper's explosion.
Sky (block): Sky is a joke block added in Java Edition 25w14craftmine.
Slab: A slab is a half-height version of its respective block.
Slime Block: A slime block is a storage block equivalent to nine slimeballs. It has both sticky and bouncy properties making it useful in conjunction with pistons to move both blocks and entities. It can be used to brew Potions of Oozing.
Small Dripleaf: A  small dripleaf is a plant which generates in lush caves, and is used to grow big dripleaves, a platforming block.
Smithing Table: A smithing table is a utility block used to apply smithing templates to tools, weapons, and armor. It also serves as a toolsmith's job site block.
Smoker: A smoker is a block that cooks food twice as quickly as a furnace, but cannot smelt anything else. It also serves as a butcher's job site block.
Smooth Basalt: Smooth basalt is an ornamental rock smelted from basalt or found as part of amethyst geodes and ancient cities.
Smooth Quartz Block: A smooth quartz block is a mineral block used only for decoration. It is made by smelting blocks of quartz.
Smooth Quartz Slab: A smooth quartz slab is a decorative slab variant of smooth quartz that generates in bastion remnants and is used for building.
Smooth Quartz Stairs: Smooth quartz stairs are a decorative stairs variant of smooth quartz that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Smooth Red Sandstone: Smooth red sandstone is a variant of red sandstone, obtained by smelting.
Smooth Red Sandstone Slab: A smooth red sandstone slab is a decorative slab variant of smooth red sandstone that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Smooth Red Sandstone Stairs: Smooth red sandstone stairs are a decorative stairs variant of smooth red sandstone that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Smooth Sandstone: Smooth sandstone is a variant of sandstone, obtained by smelting sandstone.
Smooth Sandstone Slab: A smooth sandstone slab is a decorative slab variant of smooth sandstone that generates in desert villages and is used for building.
Smooth Sandstone Stairs: Smooth sandstone stairs are a decorative stairs variant of smooth sandstone that generate in desert villages and are used for building.
Smooth Stone: Smooth stone is a variant of stone made by smelting regular stone.
Smooth Stone Bricks: Smooth stone bricks were an unobtainable variant of stone bricks, to which they visually appeared the same.
Smooth Stone Slab: A smooth stone slab is a decorative slab variant of smooth stone that generates in overworld structures and is used for building.
Sniffer Egg: A sniffer egg is a block that can be brushed out of suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins, or obtained by breeding two sniffers. It slowly hatches into a snifflet (baby sniffer) when placed.
Snow: Snow is a ground cover and gravity-affected‌[Bedrock Edition  only] block found on the surface in snowy biomes. It can be replenished during snowfall.
Snow Block: A snow block is a full-sized block of snow.
Solid block: Solid blocks consist of any type of block that has a collision box that players, mobs, or other entities cannot simply move through, and have to move on top of it or around it. Solid blocks are significantly different from liquid or gas blocks, through which entities can freely pass.
Soul Campfire: Soul campfires are dimmer variants of campfires. Soul campfires deal more damage than normal campfires and have turquoise flames. Just like normal campfires, they can be used to cook food, pacify bees, or act as a spread-proof light source, smoke signal, or damaging trap block.
Soul Fire: Soul fire is a dimmer turquoise variation of fire that is created when soul sand or soul soil is ignited. Soul fire deals more damage than normal fire and does not spread.
Soul Lantern: The soul lantern is a block that emits light. It is a variant of the lantern crafted from the soul torch.
Soul Sand: Soul sand is a block found primarily in the Nether that slows down entities walking on it unless they are wearing Soul Speed boots. It can also be used to grow Nether wart, create soul fire, and make upward bubble columns.
Soul Soil: Soul soil is a block found abundantly in soul sand valleys. It does not slow down entities, but still activates Soul Speed. It can also be used to create soul fire, and generate basalt when paired with blue ice and lava.
Soul Torch: Soul torches are non-solid blocks that emit light. They are a variant of the torch crafted with the addition of soul soil or soul sand.
Spawn Block: Spawn Block was a block that could be used by players in MinecraftEdu to set the world spawn point.
Sponge: A sponge is a block that can be placed to remove water in an area around itself. This turns it into a wet sponge, which can be smelted or placed in the Nether to dry it to be reused. Sponges can only be found in ocean monuments.
Spore Blossom: A spore blossom is a ceiling-hanging decorative block that generates in lush caves and emits green particles.
Spruce Sapling: A spruce sapling is a variant of sapling that grows into spruce and pines.
Stained Glass: Stained glass is a dyed variant of the glass block.
Stained Glass Pane: A stained glass pane is a dyed version of a glass pane. It is a transparent block that can be used as a more efficient alternative to stained glass blocks.
Stained Terracotta: Stained terracotta is a dyed variant of terracotta obtained by crafting undyed terracotta with dyes. Some of the variants are found in badlands biomes, and all variants can be smelted into glazed terracotta.
Stairs: Stairs are blocks that allow mobs and players to change elevation without jumping.
Steppe dirt: Steppe dirt was a block in MinecraftEdu. It was a purely decorative soil block, with no functionality.[verify]
Steppe sand: Steppe sand was a block in MinecraftEdu. It was a purely decorative soil block, with no functionality.[verify]
Sticky Piston: A sticky piston is a variant of the piston that can additionally pull most blocks when it retracts.
Stone: Stone is a block found underground in the Overworld or on the surface of mountains.
Stone Brick Slab: A stone brick slab is a decorative slab variant of stone bricks that generates in overworld structures and is used for building.
Stone Brick Stairs: Stone brick stairs are a decorative stairs variant of stone bricks that generate in overworld structures and are used for building.
Stone Brick Wall: A stone brick wall is a decorative wall variant of stone bricks that generates in ruined portals and is used for building.
Stone Bricks: Stone bricks are a block found in various structures. It has three other variants: mossy stone bricks, cracked stone bricks, and chiseled stone bricks.
Stone Button: A stone button is a variant of the button, a non-solid block that produces a temporary redstone signal when pressed by a player or when hit by a wind charge.
Stone Pressure Plate: A stone pressure plate is a stone variant of the pressure plate that can detect only players and mobs.
Stone Slab: A stone slab is a decorative slab variant of stone that generates in ruined portals and is used for building.
Stone Stairs: Stone stairs are a decorative stairs variant of stone used for building.
Stonecutter: A stonecutter is a block used to easily craft many stone and copper blocks, and is cheaper than normal crafting for stairs and copper variants. It is also a job site block for mason villagers.
Stonecutter (old): The stonecutter is an unused decorative block. It was previously used to craft many stone items in Pocket Edition Alpha and the Windows 10 Edition Beta until its functionality was moved to the crafting table. It was later replaced by a new stonecutter in the Creative inventory, but it still exists in old worlds which had one.
String: String is an item that can be used as a crafting material or placed as tripwire to allow tripwire hooks and observers to detect entities that touch it.
Stripped Log: A stripped log or stripped stem is a variant of the log and stem, obtained by using an axe on a log or a stem respectively. Once stripped, it cannot be reversed.
Stripped Wood: Stripped wood or stripped hyphae is a variant of wood obtained when any axe is used on wood or hyphae respectively.
Strong Roots: Strong roots are a joke block only present in 24w14potato.
Structure Block: A structure block is used to generate structures manually. They can also be used to save and load structures, alongside structure void blocks.
Structure Void: A structure void is an invisible block that is not saved by structure blocks, allowing for the creation of structures that leave some existing blocks unchanged when loaded.
Sugar Cane: Sugar cane is a plant that can only be placed on plantable blocks adjacent to water. It grows up to three blocks tall over time, but will instead uproot itself if its water is removed. Sugar cane can be crafted into sugar and paper.
Sulfur: Sulfur is a block that naturally generates in sulfur caves alongside cinnabar, in sulfur pools, and as part of sulfur springs.
Sulfur Brick Slab: A sulfur brick slab is a decorative slab variant of sulfur bricks.
Sulfur Brick Stairs: Sulfur brick stairs are a decorative stairs variant of sulfur bricks.
Sulfur Brick Wall: A sulfur brick wall is a decorative wall variant of sulfur bricks.
Sulfur Bricks: Sulfur bricks are a decorative brick variant of sulfur.
Sulfur Slab: A sulfur slab is a decorative slab variant of sulfur.
Sulfur Spike:
Sulfur spikes are blocks found in sulfur caves that form stalactites and stalagmites.
Stalactites (which point downward) grow over time when attached from underneath sulfur and can serve as falling projectiles.
Stalagmites (which point upward) do not deal extra fall damage, unlike pointed dripstone.
Sulfur Stairs: Sulfur stairs are a decorative stairs variant of sulfur used for building.
Sulfur Wall: A sulfur wall is a decorative wall variant of sulfur used for building.
Sunflower: A sunflower is a tall flower that generates exclusively in sunflower plains biomes. It can be crafted into two yellow dye.
Suspicious Gravel: Suspicious gravel is a fragile gravity-affected block found in various Overworld structures. It can be brushed to extract unique structure-dependent loot from it. It drops nothing if it breaks, and will break if it falls or is moved.
Suspicious Sand: Suspicious sand is a fragile gravity-affected block found in various Overworld structures. It can be brushed to extract unique structure-dependent loot from it. It drops nothing if it breaks, and will break if it falls or is moved.
Swaggiest stairs ever: The swaggiest stairs ever is an April Fools' joke block. It is a netherite block variant of stairs, added in Java Edition 20w14∞.
Sweet Berries:
Sweet berries are a food item obtained from sweet berry bushes and are used to plant them.
Sweet berry bushes are quick-growing plants that grow sweet berries. Players and most mobs are slowed down and take constant damage while moving through them. They can be found naturally in taiga and snowy taiga biomes.
TNT:
TNT is an explosive block that can be lit by a redstone signal, flint and steel, stray fire, flaming projectile or explosion.
When lit, TNT becomes primed TNT, a gravity-affected entity that produces a damaging, block-destroying explosion, usually after four seconds. Blocks destroyed by TNT always drop their usual items as if mined by a player.
Tall Dry Grass: Tall dry grass is the tall variant of dry grass. Unlike other tall variants of foliage, this block is only one-block tall. It generates frequently in deserts and all types of badlands, and looks like a more full version of short dry grass. It also grows on sand and terracotta, and can be eaten by sheep.
Tall Grass: Tall grass is the 2-block tall variant of short grass.
Target: A target is a block that produces a temporary redstone signal when hit by a projectile. Unlike most other conductive blocks, it also redirects adjacent redstone dust toward it.
Taterstone: Taterstone is a common block found in the Potato dimension. It is dropped when mining potone in 24w14potato.
Taterstone Slab: A taterstone slab is a taterstone variant of a slab, added in 24w14potato.
Taterstone Stairs: Taterstone stairs are a taterstone variant of the stairs, added in 24w14potato.
Taterstone Wall: A taterstone wall is a taterstone variant of a wall, added in 24w14potato.
Technical blocks: Technical blocks are blocks that can be used for some purposes when events in the game are happening, or blocks that use independent ID namespaces prevent the unnecessary combinations of block states. Technical blocks can't normally be obtained in the game, but in older Java Edition versions and current Bedrock Edition versions, different technical blocks can be obtained using glitches or NBT editing.
Teleport Block: A teleport block was a block in MinecraftEdu.
Terracotta: Terracotta is a block that is found abundantly in badlands biomes, or can be obtained by smelting clay. It can be dyed to create stained terracotta.
Terre de Pomme: Terre de pomme is a common dirt-type block found throughout the Potato dimension in 24w14potato.
Test Block: A test block is a technical block that is used for game tests.
Test Instance Block: A test instance block is a technical block that is used for game tests.
Tile.deprecated purpur block 2.name: tile.deprecated_purpur_block_2.name, presumably intended to be named smooth purpur, is an unobtainable block in the purpur family, which appears identical to standard purpur blocks.
Tinted Glass: Tinted glass is a block that blocks light while being visually transparent.
Torch: Torches are non-solid blocks that emit light.
Torch (Burnt-out): The torch (burnt-out) is a joke feature introduced exclusively in Java Edition 2.0. They are created when a normal torch burns out.
Torchflower: A torchflower is an ancient flower obtained from harvesting torchflower seeds. It can be crafted into orange dye.
Torchflower Seeds: Torchflower seeds are ancient seeds that have a chance to be dropped by sniffers when they finish digging. It is the seed of torchflowers.
Trapdoor: A trapdoor is a solid block that can be used as an openable 1×1 barrier.
Trapped Chest:
A trapped chest is a type of chest that functions almost identically, but has a red-tinted latch and produces redstone power while open.
Like normal chests, two trapped chests can merge into a large trapped chest if placed next to each other.
Trial Spawner:
A trial spawner is a type of spawner found in trial chambers. It spawns mobs in waves, ejects consumable items and/or trial keys after they are all defeated, and then deactivates for 30 minutes. Having more Survival/Adventure mode players nearby results in more mobs and more rewards.
A trial spawner will convert into an active ominous trial spawner during an ominous trial, even if it was on cooldown.
Triple Compressed Poisonous Potato Block: A triple compressed poisonous potato block is a compacted block made of double compressed poisonous potato blocks in 24w14potato.
Tripwire Hook: A tripwire hook is a block used to create a tripwire circuit, which requires two hooks and a straight horizontal line of 1-40 string. Both hooks in a valid circuit emit a redstone signal and power their attached blocks while any of the string is being touched by an entity, or if any string is broken without using shears.
Tuff: Tuff is an ornamental rock, occurring in underground ore blobs below Y=0.
Tuff Brick Slab: A tuff brick slab is a decorative slab variant of tuff bricks that does not generate naturally and is commonly used for building.
Tuff Brick Stairs: Tuff brick stairs are a decorative stairs variant of tuff bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Tuff Brick Wall: A tuff brick wall is a decorative wall variant of tuff bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Tuff Bricks: Tuff bricks are a brick variant of tuff found abundantly in trial chambers.
Tuff Slab: A tuff slab is a decorative slab variant of tuff that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Tuff Stairs: Tuff stairs are a decorative stairs variant of tuff used for building.
Tuff Wall: A tuff wall is a decorative wall variant of tuff that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
Tulip: Tulips are a kind of flower found in plains and flower forests that come in multiple colored variants: red, orange, white, and pink. They yield dyes of their respective colors, with the exception of white tulips, which yield light gray dye, and all of them are used to craft suspicious stew.
Turtle Egg: A turtle egg is a block that can be placed up to four times within one block space that hatches turtles.
Twisting Vines: Twisting vines are climbable upward-growing vegetation blocks found in the Nether in warped forests.
Underwater TNT: Underwater TNT is a block that can be used by the player to initiate a controlled explosion underwater.
USB Charger Block: The USB charger block was a joke variant of the block of redstone introduced in Java Edition 1.RV-Pre1.
Underwater Torch: The underwater torch is a non-solid block that emits light underwater.
Unknown:
Unknown is a placeholder block exclusive to Bedrock Edition that generates in place where blocks have an invalid ID or invalid components in their behavior files.
If the block has a unique model, it takes the shape of that model.
Vault: A vault is a block found in trial chambers that ejects loot when unlocked using a trial key. Each vault can be opened by an unlimited number of players, but each player can unlock a specific vault only once.
Vicious Potato: A vicious potato is a joke block added in 24w14potato. It can be found in the Potato dimension.
Vines: Vines are climbable non-solid vegetation blocks that grow on walls.
Wall: A wall is a decorative block. Like fences, they can be used to create boundaries, because players and most mobs cannot climb or jump over them.
Warped Fungus: A warped fungus is a mushroom-like block that generates in the Nether.
Warped Nylium: Warped nylium is a variant of netherrack that generates in the Nether.
Warped Roots: Warped roots are a non-solid "plant" block which generate naturally on warped nylium and soul soil in warped forests. They resemble a colony of tall, thin mushrooms.
Warped Wart Block: Warped wart blocks are a decorative block found in warped forests, generating as part of huge warped fungus.
Wart Block: Wart blocks are blocks that generate as part of huge fungi in the Nether. There are two variants, nether wart blocks, a craftable variant found in crimson forests, and warped wart blocks, an uncraftable variant found in warped forests.
Water: Water is a fluid that naturally generates abundantly in the Overworld.
Water Spawner: The water spawner was a block that would repeatedly create water on each of its four orthogonal sides.
Weak Roots: Weak roots are a joke block added in 24w14potato.
Weeping Vines: Weeping vines are climbable, downwards-growing vegetation blocks found in the Nether in crimson forests.
Wheat Seeds:
Wheat seeds are items obtained by breaking grass, or more abundantly harvested from wheat crops, and are used to plant them.
Wheat crops are planted in farmland and used to grow wheat and wheat seeds.
Wildflowers: Wildflowers are a thin decorative flower that can be placed four times in the space of one block, similar to pink petals and leaf litter.
Wither Rose: A wither rose is a damaging flower that drops when a mob is killed by a wither.
Wither Skeleton Skull: A wither skeleton skull is the head of a wither skeleton in the form of a block, which is a rare drop from killed wither skeletons. Three of them can be used to summon a wither, a destructive boss mob that is the only source of Nether stars.
Wood: Wood or hyphae is a block that has the log's "bark" texture on all six sides. It comes in 11 types: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, crimson, warped, and pale oak.
Wooden Button: A wooden button is a type of button that remains pressed for longer than a stone button and can additionally be pressed by arrows and thrown tridents.
Wooden Door: The wooden door is a variant of the door made of wood that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
Wooden Fence: A wooden fence is the wooden variant of fences, crafted using planks and sticks.
Wooden Pressure Plate: A wooden pressure plate is a wooden variant of the pressure plate. It can detect all entities, producing the maximum signal strength of 15. Wooden pressure plates come in all variants of wood.
Wooden Slab: A wooden slab is a wooden variant of a slab crafted from its respective planks.
Wooden Stairs: Wooden stairs are a wooden variant of stairs, crafted from their respective planks.
Wooden Trapdoor: A wooden trapdoor is a variant of the trapdoor that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
Wool: Wool is a block obtained from sheep that can be dyed in any of the sixteen different colors. It can be used as a crafting material and to block vibrations.
XOR Block:
In the first version of Minecraft 4k, there is only one block, with a block ID of 1. Its texture resembles that of an XOR fractal.
It seems to be a test block, as it was removed in version 4k-2 when more blocks were added.
Zombie Head: A zombie head is the head of a zombie in the form of a block. It can only be obtained by killing a zombie using a charged creeper's explosion.
